title: Spaghetti alle Vongole
subtitle: Neapolitan spaghetti with clams
excerpt: One of Italy's greatest pasta dishes: spaghetti tossed with clams cooked briefly in white wine, garlic, and olive oil, the clam juices emulsified into the pasta water to make a light, briny sauce. Simple and magnificent.

recipe.sourceNotes: Spaghetti alle vongole is one of the most celebrated pasta dishes in Italian cooking, particularly associated with the seafood traditions of Naples and the Campania coast. The dish comes in two versions: in bianco (white, without tomato) and in rosso (red, with tomato); the bianco version is the purer and more widely regarded. The technique involves opening the clams in white wine and garlic in a covered pan, then tossing the spaghetti with the cooking juices to create a sauce through emulsification. The starchy pasta water is the key emulsifier that brings together the olive oil and clam juices into a cohesive, glossy sauce. The most important rule is not to overcook the clams; they should just open and be removed from the heat immediately.

content.text: Soak the clams in cold salted water for 30 minutes before cooking to purge any grit. Reserve at least a ladleful of pasta cooking water before draining; the starch is what emulsifies the sauce. The clams open within 2 to 3 minutes; remove the pan from the heat the moment the last one opens.

items.preparation: live; scrubbed; soaked in salted cold water 30 minutes; drained

content.text: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until 2 minutes from done (al dente). Reserve at least 200 ml of the cooking water. Drain.

While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large pan. Gently fry the garlic and chilli for 1 minute without colouring. Add the wine and bring to a boil. Add the clams, cover, and cook over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until all are open. Discard any that remain closed.

Add the drained pasta to the clams. Toss over medium heat, adding pasta water a splash at a time to create a glossy, emulsified sauce that coats the pasta. Add the parsley. Serve immediately in warm bowls.
